name: Accelerated production and exploration
definition: Participants describe or appraise faster production and exploration of architectural or technical material, including advice, research code, specifications, documentation, technical options and codebase understanding.
inclusion_criteria: Reported production/exploration and explicit opinions about these benefits. Preserve task, organizational context and account type; speed claims need no implication of measured gains.
exclusion_criteria: Net efficiency and correction costs belong to K02; verification processes to K03. Do not assume all artifact types or projects become faster.
qualifications: The original contextual qualifications still apply. I4 extends investigation to large undocumented systems and describes specification generation; I6 reports technology-option exploration. I5’s documentation claims are opinions, not industrial outcomes. K02/K18 qualify speed benefits.

name: Qualified efficiency gains
definition: Perceived initial speed gains may be offset or left uncertain by interpreting, correcting and validating generated output; a complex solution can cost more effort than direct work.
inclusion_criteria: Initial generation speed alongside accuracy or end-to-end-effort qualifications, and reported unsuccessful complex-output attempts.
exclusion_criteria: Do not infer measured end-to-end gains. Verification activity itself is K03; responsibility for review is K04.
qualifications: E007 is a colleague report with the participant’s own appraisal, including an unmeasured 80% estimate. E012 is a direct failed-use case; both are retained within this broader code.

name: Verification around AI-assisted work
definition: AI-assisted work involves verification and refinement: GenAI can cross-check human work, while people or assisted workflows check generated output, architectural alignment and behavior. Reported checking, proposed assurance mechanisms and future expectations remain distinct.
inclusion_criteria: Second opinions, tests and correction; architecture-level/team review, conformance/traceability checks, fitness functions and runtime observations; distinguish proposed automated assurance from reported operational use. Checking includes scrutiny of the evidence behind generated answers and perceived limitations of AI-based checking, such as agreement with the questioner. Preserve specific failure modes as properties; they do not demonstrate calibrated trust or a reliable checking mechanism.
exclusion_criteria: Responsibility/approval is K04; encoding reasoning so it can be checked is K25; no suggestion or nested-AI checking scheme establishes proven safety or correctness.
qualifications: Earlier current/normative/future checking distinctions remain. I10 describes staged team reviews; I9 proposes fitness functions/observability and I11 proposes traceability or nested checking. I12 argues the same testing regimen can apply to human/AI code; these are not independent safety guarantees.
